skills.name: acp-interop-mapping
skills.description: Use when a partner speaks a different receipt or checkout shape (ACP, x402, CGCR/1) and you need a structural mapping that names exactly what is lost, plus deterministic vectors to test their implementation.
skills.intro: Move records between profiles without pretending the mapping is lossless.
whenToUse: A partner (agent commerce platform, gateway, marketplace) asks for receipts in their shape.
You are integrating an SDK and need test vectors that match the enforcer, not your reading of the spec.
A dispute needs the same record expressed in two profiles.

skills.name: agent-purchase-guard
skills.description: Use when an agent is about to spend money, submit an order, or sign a payment authorization, and you need the approval bound to exact bytes and the execution verified before anything is called successful.
skills.intro: Bind the buyer's approval to the order bytes, then verify what actually executed against that receipt. Offline, deterministic, fail-closed.
whenToUse: An agent is about to place an order, pay an invoice, settle an x402 challenge, or call a merchant API that moves value.
You need a receipt a human (or a dispute process) can re-derive later without trusting your logs.
A verifier, firewall, or marketplace asks "was this execution covered by an approval?".

skills.name: agent-spend-control
skills.description: Use when setting, reviewing, or explaining an agent's spending limits — compile the policy, simulate the month, prove the boundary cases, and project runway without touching production state.
skills.intro: Make the policy explicit, testable and explainable before an agent spends against it.

skills.name: incident-freeze-drill
skills.description: Use when an agent must be stopped immediately — freeze it, reject its open approvals in one audited operation, then reconstruct the timeline for review.
skills.intro: Contain first, explain second. The kill switch must be one deterministic call, and the resulting ledger must be readable.
whenToUse: A verification failed, a receipt was replayed, or a tool description was poisoned.
An owner says "stop this agent now".
You are rehearsing incident response before an agent goes live (do this drill monthly).

skills.name: mcp-server-due-diligence
skills.description: Use before installing, pinning, or approving a third-party MCP server, to turn its published manifest into a deterministic risk card a reviewer can act on.
skills.intro: Read the record before you run the code. This skill produces evidence, not a verdict on the vendor.
whenToUse: An MCP client, marketplace, or platform is about to list or install a server.
A team asks "is this server safe to add to our agent?".
You need a repeatable pre-install check that does not depend on the vendor's marketing page.

skills.name: merchant-impersonation-check
skills.description: Use when an agent is about to pay a merchant, domain, or package whose name resembles a known brand, or when a payment instruction arrives from a new domain.
skills.intro: Catch homoglyph, mixed-script and punycode impersonation before value moves.

skills.name: receipt-forensics
skills.description: Use when reconstructing what happened to a payment or approval — redact a receipt for sharing, verify an evidence bundle, and prove a record is included in a notarised batch.
skills.intro: Answer "what exactly was approved, what executed, and can we prove it later?" without a network or a trust root.

skills.name: tool-poisoning-triage
skills.description: Use when tool descriptions or prompts look off, arrive from an untrusted MCP server, or an agent starts behaving as if it received instructions the user never gave.
skills.intro: Find hidden instructions in tool metadata before the model obeys them.

skills.name: tool-surface-drift-watch
skills.description: Use on every MCP server upgrade or re-connect to detect rug pulls — tools added, removed, re-described or re-schema'd after the surface was approved.
skills.intro: An agent approved a tool surface, not a vendor. Verify the surface is still the one that was approved.
whenToUse: A dependency bump changes an MCP server version.
A hosted server reconnects and `tools/list` may differ from yesterday.
A marketplace re-scans a listing (`rescan`) and needs to show what changed.

skills.name: x402-payment-gate
skills.description: Use when an agent answers an HTTP 402 payment challenge — parse the challenge, authorize against policy, verify settlement evidence, and reconcile the payment without custody.
skills.intro: A deterministic gate for x402-style challenges: parse, authorize, verify, reconcile. No wallet, no broadcast, no custody.

boundary: Wave 3 is deterministic, offline reasoning over caller-supplied JSON: it checks structure, policy arithmetic and byte-level provenance, never truth, safety, identity or settlement. A finding is evidence for a human decision, not a verdict on a third party. VERIFIED ≠ SAFE; no network calls, no keys, no wall clock in any commitment.
